artifacts.summary: Confirms GATE 17 scoped-commit lint false positive at test-detect-noop-bash.sh:152 (fix: reword fixture to 'git commit --message "true"'); finds GATE 20 SUB-CHECK B eager-load regression is currently PASSING (65257 B vs 65950 B baseline, 693 B headroom), contradicting the dispatch's stated 66026 B figure -- traced as a stale config note, not a live regression. Recommends against a speculative trim and documents re-verification steps.

memory_candidates.content: lint-scoped-commit-boundary.sh's CANDIDATE_PATTERN='git commit -m' is a plain substring match (grep -F), so any new test fixture file under agent-system/extensions/ that embeds the literal text 'git commit -m' as inert string data (e.g. testing a classifier hook against realistic command strings) will trip this lint unless it ends in a trailing '-- <pathspec>' or is added to the file-level EXCLUDED_FILES allowlist. Prefer rewording the fixture (e.g. 'git commit -m' -> 'git commit --message', git's documented long-form equivalent) over allowlisting the whole file, when the fixture's test intent does not depend on the exact '-m' spelling.

orchestrator-context-budget.json's eager_load.measured_bytes/measured_at/note fields are purely informational -- verify-deploy.sh's Gate 20 Sub-check B reads only eager_load.baseline_bytes via jq. A recorded measured_bytes figure in that config's note can go stale or be wrong at the moment it was written (verified case: a commit's own note claimed 66026 B but a git-archive re-run of measure-eager-context.sh --check against that exact commit reproduced 65257 B instead). Before trusting a task description's stated eager-load byte figures, re-run 'REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bash agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/measure-eager-context.sh --check' fresh rather than assuming a config note's recorded number is still accurate.
